correctness.rationale: The weighted Kirchhoff cofactor is reconstructed as a Schur complement and directly generates the conditional binomial degree law. A nested-support binomial adjacent-ratio comparison proves every reverse TP2 minor, including support boundaries. The exact symmetrization and covariance identities follow algebraically from the known Cayley total count and unconditional Prüfer degree law. Contat Theorems 1 and 2 supply the only imported asymptotic premises, cited rather than re-proved. An independently generated Prüfer enumerator and rational checker passed 203981 assertions. No finite computation was treated as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Contat (2021) proves the marginal parity-class law, its local Gaussian limit and near-symmetry; Féray–Kortchemski (2017/2018) prove two-type population-count identities. Those results do not themselves state a root-degree-refined joint distribution, reverse likelihood-ratio ordering, or the limiting residual covariance. The known weighted spanning-tree product is not claimed as new. Actual semantic searches found no dominating statement in the checked records. A possible implicit classical bicolored-tree refinement remains a historical-priority risk.

value.rationale: The questions of how root-local degree predicts a global parity-class size and whether the two statistics decorrelate are naturally motivated by bicolored Cayley trees. The complete reverse-TP2 inequality governs all pairs of increasing test functions at every size, not one covariance. The exact symmetrization identifies a nonzero unscaled covariance limit even though the normalized variable and degree converge to independent Gaussian and shifted-Poisson laws, distinguishing weak from moment-level asymptotic independence.
